context: Short term the fix is one line in anonymization_specs.yaml, but a second hand-synced list is still a hand-synced list - it diverged within a month of #1346. Prefer making both consumers read ONE source of truth (either platform_options derives from the spec file, or both derive from a shared module) and pin it with the list-consistency rung below. See the credential-egress RCA: name-based matching is a backstop, not the mechanism, so do not expand this into a redesign here.
description: Two secret-key lists that must agree do not. platform_options.py:20 _SECRET_KEY_PARTS contains 'keyid' (added by PR #1346); anonymization_specs.yaml secret_key_parts does not. anonymization.py:36 loads that spec and anonymization.py:360 _is_secret_metadata_key() matches against it. Measured 2026-07-31 on develop 8c9d7f8d8 by driving the real entry point: anonymize_result_payload({'platform_metadata':{'platform_raw_config':{'s3_key_id':'AKIA-SENTINEL'}}}) returns the sentinel VERBATIM, while pg_password becomes '<redacted>' and username is pseudonymized to user_<hash>. SCOPE OF EXPOSURE (corrected from the first draft of this item, which overstated it): in the normal capture path sanitize_platform_options runs first and already returns s3_key_id='<redacted>', so the anonymization gap is masked upstream there. It bites where raw platform metadata reaches anonymization without that pre-pass - re-export of loaded or historical result bundles is the plausible case. So this is defence-in-depth degradation plus a conditional live leak, not an unconditional one. Still high: anonymization is the LAST stage before publication and is the only thing standing between a raw payload and published results.

preserves.behavior: Existing anonymization behavior for already-covered keys (pg_password redacted, username pseudonymized)
sanitize_platform_options keeps redacting everything it does today
